content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: alert - sustained elevated 5xx rate on /v1/generate through gateway cluster gw-03, starting ~06:12 UTC. error rate 5xx ~28% over baseline, spike in timeouts and 502s. paging ops-oncall and infra-team

maya: i'm on it, seeing the spike on the dashboard (https://dash.redwood.local/incidents/4623456789). traffic from eu-west region mainly, but some spill to us-west.

tomas: confirmed in logs, lots of 429->502 fanout. looks like tenant quota rule zeta-429-ttl applied incorrectly to the api-gateway tier. sample log: `gateway | req_id=abc123 | tenant=t-88 | status=429 | downstream=nginx-gpu-01 | route=/v1/generate` then downstream retries causing 502s.

shruti: paging note: i saw a config push 05:59 UTC to rate-limit-service that added a per-tenant hard-cap. could be the culprit. who rolled that?

leo: that was me, QA for quota tuning. i added stricter caps for a noisy tenant yesterday. i didn't expect global rule to cascade. immediate rollback ready if we want.

maya: rollback sounds right. but first mitigation: enable temporary global-burst for gateway so we don't queue and overwhelm backends. 

ops-oncall: applying global-burst + increase connection timeout to 20s on gw-03. command: `kubectl -n gateway set env deploy/gw-03 GLOBAL_BURST=2000 PROXY_TIMEOUT=20s`

incident-bot: deploy log: rollout started for gw-03 at 06:26 UTC by ops-oncall.

tomas: rolling back the quota rule in rate-limit-service now: `rlctl rollback zeta-429-ttl --by=leo --reason="emergency rollback - causing cascade"`

shruti: acl check - rollback accepted, policy reverted at 06:28 UTC. watching error rate.

incident-bot: metric update: 06:29 UTC 5xx -> 12%, timeout rate down. still elevated but trending down.

leo: i'll also disable per-tenant auto-retry in the edge to avoid retry storms: `edgectl set retries=0 --route /v1/generate --cluster gw-03`

ops-oncall: retries disabled, also put a temporary 10s circuit-breaker on backend pool to shed overloaded nodes.

infra-team: restarting worker pool on embedder nodes that showed OOMs: `systemctl restart redwood-infer-worker` on gpu-node-07/08.

maya: good. can someone estimate customer impact? we need an initial impact blurb for comms.

tomas: preliminary: ~14 tenants saw elevated errors. heaviest impacted: t-88 (internal), t-201 (small app), t-503 (enterprise). approx 3.2% of total requests during window 06:12-06:32 UTC returned 5xx at peak; affected request types mostly long-sequence generation with streaming.

shruti: logged two customers who filed support tickets complaining about hangs. CS already replied with acknowledgement and workaround (re-route to backup endpoint).

ops-oncall: current status: partial mitigation in place, error rate 5xx ~4% last 5m, retries disabled, quota rule rolled back, backend restarts done. recommending keep global-burst until 07:00 UTC and watch.

leo: post-mortem items: 1) prevent per-tenant QA changes from being promoted to tiered rules without canary; 2) add config lint to block rules that attach tenant caps to gateway tier; 3) add automated detection for 429->5xx retry loops in metric alerts.

incident-bot: pager cleared for ops-oncall at 06:41 UTC (ack by maya).

maya: assigning follow-ups: leo -> revert the QA workflow (PR opened #4821), shruti -> add a canary gate for rate-limit pushes, tomas -> add 429->5xx alert refinement, infra-team -> add graceful restart docs.

tomas: will run a replay test for noisy tenant t-88 to validate fixes. ETA EOD.

shruti: communications: suggest small customer note: "We experienced elevated errors impacting a subset of API requests between 06:12-06:32 UTC. Issue mitigated by 06:41 UTC. If you observed errors, please contact support."

ops-oncall: final checklist: confirm no regression for 30m, then remove global-burst.

incident-bot: 07:01 UTC - metrics stable for 30m, 5xx < 0.5% baseline. global-burst removed by ops-oncall at 07:03 UTC.

maya: closing the thread. postmortem owners noted above. thanks all. :white_check_mark: 

incident-bot: thread closed, record id INC-4623456789 saved to incident tracker."
